annotations.title: Park an incident after a fix or a verdict

description: Take a firing incident off the live wall into the Parked section, for at most 72 hours (more is refused, not shortened), once you have FIXED it or reached a VERDICT on it. `state`: fixed_undeployed (the fix is merged and not live yet), awaiting_source (the fix is live and the source's evaluation window has not caught up, so it still reports the alert), deferred (a person decided to handle it at a later date; the note says who and why). It works for any source, Grafana included. Unlike `resolve` it never reopens or pages while the park holds, and unlike `silence` it states a known cause: the tile reads "Parked until <time> by <you>" with your note, it counts as parked and not firing, and nothing is sent. It ends when the source resolves the alert, when `until` passes (the incident comes back unattended and its clock counts from `until`, so the pager treats it as a new problem), on `unpark`, or on a manual `resolve`; an acknowledgement or silence on the incident still wins over it, and a second park replaces the first. Park only after a fix or a verdict, never to hide a live problem you have not looked at or to quiet one you cannot explain. The park covers only the alerts firing when you park (get_incident lists their keys in `park.alertKeys`): an alert that joins the incident later (another host or instance, a new rule on it) ends the park at once, the incident comes back unattended and pages as a new problem, and History says which alert joined. An alert that resolves and fires again keeps the park.

by.description: Who is doing this, as "agent: <who>", for example "agent: claude in web-app". Required: it is shown on the tile, in the incident sheet and in History. "agent: " is added when left off. At most 64 characters.

key.description: The incident key exactly as watch_state or list_incidents print it ("<service>|<rule>", or "<service>|<rule>|<instance>" for a rule split per instance). Not an alert key.

note.description: Why it is parked: what you fixed or decided and how you know, at most 500 characters. Required: it is shown on the tile and in the sheet beside your name.

ref.description: A ticket, PR or commit that explains the park, one line, at most 64 characters.

state.description: Why it is parked: fixed_undeployed (the fix is merged, not live yet), awaiting_source (the fix is live, the source has not caught up), or deferred (handled at a later date).

until.description: When the park ends: an ISO 8601 time with a zone (Z or an offset), for example 2026-10-17T04:00:00Z, after now and at most 72 hours from now. More is refused, not shortened: the refusal names the latest time that is taken. Choose the shortest time that covers the fix.

name: park
title: Park an incident after a fix or a verdict
